title: From a Galloping Horse to a Moving Train: How Cinema Was Born
title_zh: 从疾驰的马到进站的火车：电影如何诞生
intro_zh: 本文约 552 词。从光学玩具、奔马实验到卢米埃尔兄弟的首次公开放映，讲述电影诞生的关键步骤。

paragraphs.en: Today we watch movies on phones and huge screens. But little more than a century ago, moving pictures did not exist. The idea that a photograph could come alive seemed impossible. Yet a few curious inventors and artists turned that dream into reality. Their experiments with light, paper and machines gave the world a new way to tell stories. No one knew it then, but a new art form was about to appear.
paragraphs.zh: 如今我们在手机和巨幕上看电影。但仅仅一个多世纪前，会动的画面还不存在。照片能活起来，这个想法似乎不可能。然而几位好奇的发明家和艺术家把这个梦想变成了现实。他们在光、纸和机器上的实验，给世界带来了一种讲述故事的新方式。当时无人知晓，但一种新的艺术形式即将出现。

paragraphs.en: The journey began with simple optical toys. In the 1830s, a device called the zoetrope used a spinning drum and paper strips. When a person looked through small holes, a series of drawings appeared to move. This was an illusion created by the human eye. The brain holds an image for a split second, so separate pictures blend into smooth action.
paragraphs.zh: 旅程始于简单的光学玩具。19世纪30年代，一种叫西洋镜的装置用旋转的鼓和纸条。当人通过小孔看时，一连串图画似乎动了起来。这是人眼产生的错觉。大脑会把一个图像保留一瞬间，所以分开的图片混合成流畅的动作。

paragraphs.en: A major step came from a bet about a horse. In 1878, the photographer Eadweard Muybridge set up 24 cameras along a racetrack in California. As a horse galloped past, it broke thin wires that triggered each camera. The result was a sequence of still photos. For the first time, people could see that all four of a horse’s feet leave the ground during a gallop. Muybridge had captured motion in separate frames. This experiment proved that photography could freeze time.
paragraphs.zh: 一个关于马的赌局带来了重大进步。1878年，摄影师埃德沃德·迈布里奇在加利福尼亚一条赛马道旁架起24台相机。当马疾驰而过，它碰断细线，依次触发每台相机。结果是一连串静态照片。人们第一次看到，马在疾驰时四蹄同时离地。迈布里奇用一个个画面捕捉了运动。这个实验证明摄影可以定格时间。

paragraphs.en: Others pushed the idea further. In 1888, a French inventor named Louis Le Prince used a single camera to record a short scene of people walking in a garden. It is often called the first film. Meanwhile, in the United States, Thomas Edison’s team built the Kinetoscope, a box that showed moving pictures to one person at a time. These early devices were exciting, but they were not yet a shared public experience.
paragraphs.zh: 其他人把这个想法推进得更远。1888年，法国发明家路易·勒普林斯用一台相机录下人们在花园里走动的短场景。它常被称为第一部电影。与此同时，在美国，托马斯·爱迪生的团队制造了电影视镜，一种一次只给一个人看活动画面的盒子。这些早期装置令人兴奋，但还不是共享的公众体验。

paragraphs.en: The real breakthrough came from two French brothers, Auguste and Louis Lumière. They invented the Cinématographe, a machine that could both take pictures and project them onto a screen. On December 28, 1895, they held the first public paid screening in Paris. About 30 people watched short films, including one of a train arriving at a station. Some in the audience were so surprised that they reportedly jumped back.
paragraphs.zh: 真正的突破来自法国两兄弟奥古斯特和路易·卢米埃尔。他们发明了电影机，一种既能拍摄又能把画面投射到银幕上的机器。1895年12月28日，他们在巴黎举行了第一次公开收费放映。大约30人观看了短片，其中一部是火车进站。据说有些观众惊讶得往后跳。

paragraphs.en: Why did this moment matter so much? Because film could do something no other art form could. It could capture the real world in motion and show it to many people at once. A play changes every night, and a painting stands still. But a film is exactly the same every time it is shown. This invention opened the door to news, education and entertainment for the masses.
paragraphs.zh: 为什么这一刻如此重要？因为电影能做到其他艺术形式做不到的事。它能捕捉运动中的真实世界，并同时展示给许多人。戏剧每晚都在变，绘画静止不动。但电影每次放映都完全相同。这项发明为大众打开了新闻、教育和娱乐的大门。

paragraphs.en: The early films were very short—often less than a minute. Cameras were heavy, and film was expensive. Yet within 20 years, filmmakers learned to tell stories with close-ups, different camera angles and editing. Small theaters called nickelodeons appeared in cities, charging just five cents for a show. Cinema was no longer a scientific curiosity; it had become a popular industry. By 1915, feature-length films were drawing millions of viewers.
paragraphs.zh: 早期电影非常短——常常不到一分钟。相机很重，胶片很贵。然而20年内，电影制作者学会了用特写、不同机位和剪辑来讲故事。城市里出现了叫五分钱影院的小电影院，看一场只要五美分。电影不再是科学奇观，它已经成为一个流行产业。到1915年，长片已经吸引了数百万观众。

paragraphs.en: From a spinning paper toy to a global art form, the birth of cinema was a chain of small discoveries. Each inventor solved one piece of the puzzle. Together, they changed how we see the world and how we share its stories. The next time you watch a film, remember the galloping horse and the arriving train that started it all.
paragraphs.zh: 从旋转的纸玩具到全球艺术形式，电影的诞生是一连串小发现。每位发明家解决了拼图的一块。他们共同改变了我们看世界以及分享故事的方式。下次你看电影时，请记住那匹疾驰的马和那列进站的火车，它们开启了一切。

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: The history of photography from 1830 to 1900.
The scientific principles behind optical toys.
How cinema developed from early experiments to a popular industry.
Why Edison and the Lumière brothers were rivals.
questions.explain: 文章从光学玩具、奔马实验、爱迪生和卢米埃尔兄弟的贡献，讲到电影成为流行产业，故主旨为电影如何从早期实验发展成为流行产业。C正确。

questions.q: According to the passage, what did Eadweard Muybridge’s experiment in 1878 show?
options: That horses can run faster than trains.
That all four of a horse’s feet leave the ground during a gallop.
That a single camera can record a horse in motion.
That photographs could be projected onto a screen.
questions.explain: 第三段明确提到，迈布里奇的实验第一次让人们看到马在疾驰时四蹄同时离地。B正确。

questions.q: What can be inferred about the first public screening by the Lumière brothers?
options: It was free for everyone to attend.
It lasted for more than an hour.
It had a strong physical effect on some viewers.
It was shown in the United States.
questions.explain: 第五段提到有些观众惊讶得往后跳，说明放映对部分观众产生了强烈的身体反应。C正确。

questions.q: The word "illusion" in Paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: illusion 意为“错觉、幻觉”，与 a false belief or perception 最接近。A正确。
